Ege Eğitim Dergisi 2015 (16) 1: 1-12
Çocuk ve Genç Psikolojik Sağlamlık Ölçeği’nin (ÇGPSÖ-12) Psikometrik Özellikleri:
Geçerlilik ve Güvenirlik Çalışması
Gökmen ARSLAN1
Geliş Tarihi: 26.11.2014 Kabul Tarihi: 16.06.2015
Bu çalışmanın amacı Çocuk ve Genç Psikolojik Sağlamlık Ölçeği’nin psikometrik özelliklerini incelemektir.
Çalışmaya Isparta il merkezinde ortaokul ve lisede öğrenim gören toplam 256 öğrenci katılmıştır.
Katılımcıların yaşları 11 ile 16 arasında değişmektedir.
Yaş ortalaması 13.05 (Ss = .97)’dir.
Katılımcıların % 44’ü kız, % 56’sı erkek öğrencilerden oluşmaktadır.
Açımlayıcı ve doğrulayıcı faktör analizi sonuçları, ölçeğin toplam varyansın % 51.28’ini açıklayan tek faktörden meydana geldiği göstermiştir.
Ölçüt geçerliliği kapsamında olumlu olumsuz duygular ve öz yeterlik le ilişkisine bakılmış, ÇGPSÖ ile öz yeterlik, olumlu duygular arasında pozitif, olumsuz duygular ile negatif yönde ve anlamlı düzeyde bir ilişkinin olduğu görülmüştür.
Güvenirlik çalışması kapsamında ölçeğe ilişkin iç tutarlılık katsayısı hesaplanmıştır.
Cronbach alpha değeri .91 olarak hesaplanmıştır.
Elde edilen bu sonuçlar Çocuk ve Genç Psikolojik Sağlamlık Ölçeği’nin ülkemizde çocuk ve ergenlerde psikolojik sağlamlığı değerlendirmede kullanılabileceğini göstermektedir.
Anahtar Kelimeler: Psikolojik sağlamlık, ergenlik, güvenirlik, geçerlilik.

Abstract
The aim of this study is to investigate the psychometric properties of Child and Youth Resilience Measure (CYRM).
The Cronbach alpha coefficient of CYRM was .91.

Giriş
Ergenlik dönemin genellikle alan yazında çocukluktan yetişkinliğe geçiş dönemi olarak ele
alınmaktadır (Steinberg, 2007).
Bu dönemde bireyde meydana gelen değişimler birey için
birtakım uyum sorunlarını beraberinde getirirken aynı zamanda yeni yaşantılar için fırsatlar
sunar.
Bu süreçte birey, gelişim sürecini ve iyi oluşunu olumsuz etkileyebilecek istismar ve
ihmal, boşanma, gibi bir takım yaşantılar ile karşı karşıya kalabilmektedir (Santrock, 2012).
Kişinin karşılaşmış olduğu bu zorluklar rağmen sağlıklı şekilde gelişim göstermesi alan
yazında psikolojik sağlamlık kavramı ile karşılık bulmaktadır (Sameroff, 2005).
Bireyin olumlu yaşantıları, duyguları, kişilik özellikleri ve deneyimleri ile güçlü
yönleri üzerine odaklanan pozitif psikolojinin ilgilendiği önemli kavramlarından biri olan
psikolojik sağlamlık kavramı, yapılan çalışmalarda gerek kavramsal gerekse metodolojik
açıdan oldukça hetrojen bir yapı göstermektedir (Nasvytienė, La zdauskas ve Leonavičienė,
2012).
Zorluklar karşısında gösterilen olumlu uyumu kapsayan ve dinamik bir süreç olarak
tanımlanan psikolojik sağlamlıkta iki önemli durum söz konusudur.
Bunlardan birincisi
önemli bir tehdide veya ciddi bir sıkıntıya maruz kalma ve diğeri de gelişimsel sürece yönelik
önemli saldırıları ve travmaları içermesine karşın olumlu uyum sağlamayı başarmadır (Luthar,
2005; Luthar, Cicchetti ve Becker, 2000; Masten, 2001; Masten ve Coatsworth, 1998).
Burada
bireyin gelişimine veya uyumuna yönelik tehditlere ya da risklere rağmen olumlu sonuçların
ortaya çıkması söz konusudur (Masten, 2001).
Ortak bir tanımdan bahsetmek güç olsa da,
yapılan tanımlardan hareketle psikolojik sağlamlığın olumsuz yaşantılar karşısında bireyin
uyum sağlayabilme ve gelişim sürecini sürdürebilme kapasitesi olduğu söylenilebilir.
Psikolojik sağlamlık kavramının çok boyutlu ve karmaşık bir yapıya sahip olması,
kavramın değerlendirilmesi ve değerlendirmeye yönelik ölçme araçlarının geliştirilmesi
konusunda önemli güçlükler doğurmaktadır (Liebenberg, Ungar ve LeBlanc, 2013).
Bu
durumun sağlam bireylerin sahip oldukları bireysel, ailesel, sosyal ve kültürel niteliklerin
belirlenmesi için farklı ölçme araçlarına gereksinim oluşturduğu söylenebilir.
Ayrıca sağlam
bireylerin özelliklerinin incelenmesi önleyici ve müdahale çalışmaları açısından oldukça
önemli yer edinmektedir.
Bu nedenle alan yazında çocuk ve ergenlerde psikolojik sağlamlığı
değerlendirmede, yeni ölçme araçlarına gereksinim olduğu görülmektedir.
Ayrıca alan yazın
incelendiğinde ülkemizde çocuk ve ergenlerde psikolojik sağlamlığı ölçmeye yönelik sınırlı
sayıda ölçme aracının olduğu görülmektedir.
Örneğin, Gizir ve Aydın (2006) tarafından
uyarlama çalışması yapılan Psikolojik Sağlamlık ve Ergen Gelişim Ölçeği, psikolojik

Sonuç olarak bu çalışmanın amacı, Çocuk ve Genç Psikolojik Sağlamlık Ölçeği’nin

Psikolojik sağlamlığı çocuk ve ergenlerde ölçmek
amacıyla ülkemizde sınırlı sayıda ölçme aracının bulunması yeni çalışmalara gereksinim

Ayrıca, var olan ölçme araçlarının madde sayılarının oldukça fazla olması

Bu

Veri Analiz Süreci
Ölçme aracına ilişkin dil geçerliliği kapsamında 12 maddeden oluşan ölçeğin orijinal İngilizce
formu, ölçeği geliştiren araştırmacıdan izin alınarak, önce araştırmacılar tarafından Türkçe’ye,
daha sonra eğitim bilimleri alanından iki öğretim üyesi tarafından Türkçe’den İngilizce ’ye
çevrilmiş, her iki dili etkili bir şekilde kullanabilen alandan üçüncü bir öğretim üyesi
tarafından çeviriler karşılaştırılarak ölçeğe son şekli verilmiştir.
Ölçme araçları 2014-2015
eğitim öğretim dönemi başında farklı ortaokul ve lisede okuyan öğrencilerden gönüllü
olanlara verilerek uygulanmıştır.
İlk olarak ili milli eğitim müdürlüğünden araştırmanın

uygulama sürecine geçilmiştir.
Uygulama öncesi katılımcılara araştırmanın amacı ve ölçme
araçları hakkında kısaca bilgi verilmiştir.
Verilerin toplanması yaklaşık bir hafta ve uygulama
30 dakika sürmüştür.
Elde edilen veriler bilgisayar ortamına aktarıldıktan sonra, yapılacak analizler için
gerekli varsayımlara bakılmıştır.
Öncelikle hatalı ve kayıp veriler, frekans dağılımları yardımı
ile incelenmiş, hatalı verilere ilişkin gerekli düzeltmeler yapılmıştır.
Kayıp değerler % 5’in

Kayıp değerler incelenmiş ve % 5 üzerinde olan 68 veri setten

Veri setine ilişkin normal dağılım durumu veya analiz sonuçlarını etkilemesi
muhtemel durumlardan kaçınmak (Seçer, 2013) için % 5 altında olan kayıp değerlere ise
aritmetik ortalama (series mean) ile değer atanmıştır.
Bir sonraki adımda veri setindeki uç
değerler ve çok değişkenli normallik varsayımının karşılanıp karşılanmadığı Mahalanobis
uzaklık değerleri yardımıyla incelenmiş ve 12 veri setten aşırı ve uç değer olmaları nedeniyle
çıkartılmıştır.
Ayrıca tek değişkenli normallik varsayımı için basıklık ve çarpıklık
katsayılarına bakılmıştır.
Basıklık ve çarpıklık değerlerinin normallik varsayımı olan +1 ve -1
aralığını (Can, 2013; Morgan, Leech, Gloeckner ve Barrett, 2004) karşıladığı görülmüştür.
Ölçme aracına ilişkin doğrulayıcı faktör analizi sonuçları, ki-kare (χ2), χ2/sd oranı,
iyilik uyum indeksi (goodness of fit index, GFI), normlaştırılmış uyum indeksi (normed fit
index, NFI), karşılaştırmalı uyum indeksi (comparative fit index, CFI), standardize edilmiş
artık ortalamaların karekökü (standardized root mean square residuals, SRMR), fazlalık uyum
belirteci (incremental fit index, IFI) ve yaklaşık hataların ortalama karekökü (root mean
square error of approximation, RMSEA) uyum indeksleri çerçevesinde değerlendirilmiştir.
χ2/sd oranının 3’ten küçük değer alması kabul edilebilir uyuma, RMSEA ve SRMR için ise
0.05’e eşit veya daha küçük değerler mükemmel bir uyuma, 0.08 ve altındaki değerler kabul
edilebilir bir uyuma karşılık gelmektedir.
GFI, CFI, TLI, NFI ve RFI ise 0 ile 1 aralığında
değişen değerler alır.
0.95 ve üzeri mükemmel uyuma, 0.90 ve 0.94 arası değerler de kabul
edilebilir uyuma karşılık gelir (Hoe, 2008; Kline, 2011; Raykov ve Marcoulides, 2006;
Şimşek, 2007).
Bu çalışma kapsamında oluşturulan modelin uygunluğu yukarıda verilen
uyum indeksleri çerçevesinde değerlendirilmiştir.
Ölçme aracına ilişkin geçerlilik ve
güvenirlik çalışması SPSS 22 ve AMOS 22 programları aracılığıyla ve .05 anlamlılık
düzeyiyle test edilmiştir.
Bulgular
Ölçme aracına ilişkin geçerlilik ve güvenirlik çalışması iki aşamadan oluşmaktadır.
Gerekli
izinler yazardan alındıktan sonra ölçme aracı Türkçeye çevrilmiştir.
Ardından ölçme aracının
faktör yapısı açımlayıcı faktör analizi (AFA) ve doğrulayıcı faktör analizi (DFA) ile
incelenmiştir.

Elde edilen sonuçlar Kaiser Meyer Olkin değerinin .92 olduğu
görülmüş, Barlett testi sonucu, (χ2= 1533,522 sd=66, p <.000) anlamlı bulunmuştur.
Bu
doğrultuda verilerin çok değişkenli normal dağılımdan geldiği ve maddeler arasında kısmi

Ölçeğin yapı geçerliğini ve faktör yapısını incelemek amacıyla açımlayıcı faktör analizi,
faktörleştirme tekniği olarak da temel bileşenler analizi uygulanmıştır.
Ölçeğin yapı
geçerliğini belirlemek için, Kaiser normalleştirmesine göre özdeğeri (eigenvalue) 1.00’in
üzerinde olan faktörler ölçüt alınmıştır.

The aim of this study is to examine the psychometric properties of the Child and Youth Psychological Resilience Scale. A total of 256 students studying in middle and high schools in the city center of Isparta participated in the study. The ages of the participants ranged from 11 to 16 years. The mean age was 13.05 (SD = .97). Of the participants, 44% were female and 56% were male students. The results of the exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses showed that the scale consists of a single factor that accounts for 51.28% of the total variance. In terms of criterion validity, relationships with positive and negative affect and self-efficacy were examined, and it was found that there was a positive and significant relationship between the Child and Youth Psychological Resilience Scale and self-efficacy and positive affect, while there was a negative and significant relationship with negative affect. As part of the reliability study, the internal consistency coefficient of the scale was calculated. The Cronbach’s alpha coefficient was found to be .91. These findings indicate that the Child and Youth Psychological Resilience Scale can be used to assess psychological resilience in children and adolescents in our country. Introduction  
The period of adolescence is generally addressed in the literature as a transitional phase from childhood to adulthood (Steinberg, 2007). The changes experienced by individuals during this period bring about certain adaptation problems, while also providing opportunities for new experiences. In this process, individuals may be faced with various experiences such as abuse, neglect, or divorce, which can negatively affect their developmental processes and well-being (Santrock, 2012). The healthy development of an individual despite these difficulties is referred to as psychological resilience in the literature (Sameroff, 2005). Psychological resilience, one of the key concepts of positive psychology— which focuses on individuals’ positive experiences, emotions, personality traits, and strengths—has been shown in the literature to exhibit considerable heterogeneity both conceptually and methodologically (Nasvytienė, La zdauskas, and Leonavičienė, 2012). Psychological resilience, defined as a dynamic process that encompasses positive adaptation in the face of adversity, involves two important conditions. The first is exposure to a significant threat or serious distress, and the second is the ability to achieve positive adaptation despite facing major developmental threats and traumas (Luthar, 2005; Luthar, Cicchetti, and Becker, 2000; Masten, 2001; Masten and Coatsworth, 1998). Here, positive outcomes emerge despite threats or risks to the individual’s development or adaptation (Masten, 2001). Although it is difficult to speak of a single definition, based on the definitions provided, psychological resilience can be said to refer to an individual’s capacity to adapt and continue their developmental process in the face of adverse experiences. The multidimensional and complex structure of the concept of psychological resilience presents significant challenges in evaluating the construct and in developing measurement tools for its assessment (Liebenberg, Ungar, and LeBlanc, 2013). It can be said that this situation necessitates the use of different measurement tools to identify the individual, familial, social, and cultural qualities of resilient individuals. In addition, examining the characteristics of resilient individuals holds a crucial place in terms of preventive and intervention studies. Therefore, it appears that there is a need for new measurement tools to assess psychological resilience in children and adolescents, as indicated in the literature. Furthermore, when the literature is reviewed, it is evident that there are only a limited number of measurement tools available in our country for assessing psychological resilience in children and adolescents. For example, the Psychological Resilience and Adolescent Development Scale, adapted by Gizir and Aydın (2006), was developed to identify protective factors related to psychological resilience. This scale, which consists of internal and external protective factors, includes 56 items. Apart from this study, no other measurement tool aimed at assessing resilience in children and adolescents could be found in the literature. In conclusion, the aim of this study is to examine the psychometric properties of the Child and Youth Psychological Resilience Scale. The limited number of measurement tools available in our country for assessing psychological resilience in children and adolescents creates the need for new studies. Additionally, the fact that existing measurement tools contain a large number of items can pose limitations for researchers working with large samples. Therefore, it can be said that new measurement tools related to psychological resilience will fill an important gap in the literature. Method  
Study Group  
The research data were obtained from 256 students attending various high schools and middle schools in the city center of Isparta. The participants’ ages ranged from 11 to 16 years, with a mean age of 13.05 (SD = .97). Of the participants, 44% were female and 56% were male students. After obtaining the necessary permissions, data collection instruments were administered in randomly selected classrooms at randomly chosen schools.  
Data Collection Instruments  
Personal Information Form: This form was prepared and administered by the researcher to determine demographic variables such as gender and age. Child and Youth Psychological Resilience Scale: The original form of the scale, developed based on data collected from eleven different countries, consists of 28 items, three subscales, and eight subdimensions. The measurement tool was developed using both quantitative and qualitative methods from a socio-ecological perspective (Liebenberg, Ungar, and Van de Vijver, 2012). The short form study of the scale was conducted by Liebenberg, Ungar, and LeBlanc (2013), and as a result of two different studies, a structure consisting of 12 items was obtained. The factor loadings of the scale range between .39 and .88, and its internal consistency coefficient was found to be .84. The measurement tool uses a five-point Likert structure, ranging from “Describes me completely (5)” to “Does not describe me at all (1).” Higher scores indicate a higher level of resilience. Self-Efficacy Scale: The Self-Efficacy Scale for Children was developed by Muris (2001) to measure the social, academic, and emotional self-efficacy of adolescents aged 12–19. The Turkish adaptation of the scale was carried out by Telef (2011). When examining the internal consistency coefficients of the Self-Efficacy Scale for Children, the coefficient was calculated as .86 for the overall scale, .84 for academic self-efficacy, .64 for social self-efficacy, and .78 for emotional self-efficacy. The test-retest reliability coefficients of the scale ranged from .75 to .89. The General Self-Efficacy Scale was used for criterion-related validity. The Pearson product-moment correlation between the scores obtained from the two scales was found to be .57. The Self-Efficacy Scale for Children is a five-point Likert-type scale (1 = not at all, 5 = very well), with a maximum possible score of 105 and a minimum score of 21. A high score on the scale indicates a high level of self-efficacy in children, while a low score indicates a low level of self-efficacy in children.  
Positive and Negative Affect Scale: The Positive and Negative Affect Scale was developed by Watson, Clark, and Tellegen to assess individuals' positive and negative emotions. The validity and reliability study in our country was conducted by Gençöz (2000). The scale consists of 10 positive and 10 negative affect items, each of which is rated on a scale from 1 to 5. In the adaptation study of the scale, Cronbach’s alpha internal consistency coefficient was found to be .83 for Negative Affect and .86 for Positive Affect. The obtained positive and negative affect scores can be used together or separately. Data Analysis Process
Within the scope of language validity for the measurement instrument, the original English form of the 12-item scale, with permission from the researcher who developed the scale, was first translated into Turkish by the researchers, and then back into English by two faculty members from the field of educational sciences. A third faculty member from the field, proficient in both languages, compared the translations and finalized the scale. The measurement instruments were administered at the beginning of the 2014–2015 academic year to volunteers among students from various middle and high schools. Initially, the necessary permissions to conduct the research were obtained from the provincial directorate of national education. Subsequently, the implementation process began in randomly selected schools. Prior to administration, participants were briefly informed about the purpose of the research and the measurement instruments. Data collection took approximately one week and the administration lasted 30 minutes. After transferring the collected data to the computer environment, the necessary assumptions for the analyses were examined. First, incorrect and missing data were reviewed with the help of frequency distributions, and the necessary corrections were made for the erroneous data. Missing values can be tolerated if they are below 5% and randomly distributed (Acuna and Rodriguez, 2004). Missing values were examined, and 68 datasets with more than 5% missing data were excluded. For missing values below 5%, values were imputed using the arithmetic mean (series mean) to avoid conditions that might affect the normal distribution status of the dataset or the analysis results (Seçer, 2013). In the next step, outliers and the assumption of multivariate normality in the dataset were examined using Mahalanobis distance values, and 12 datasets were removed due to being extreme outliers. Additionally, skewness and kurtosis coefficients were checked for the assumption of univariate normality. It was found that the skewness and kurtosis values met the normality assumption within the range of +1 and -1 (Can, 2013; Morgan, Leech, Gloeckner, and Barrett, 2004). The results of confirmatory factor analysis for the measurement instrument were evaluated within the framework of fit indices, including chi-square (χ2), χ2/df ratio, goodness of fit index (GFI), normed fit index (NFI), comparative fit index (CFI), standardized root mean square residuals (SRMR), incremental fit index (IFI), and root mean square error of approximation (RMSEA). A χ2/df ratio below 3 indicates an acceptable fit, while RMSEA and SRMR values equal to or less than 0.05 indicate a perfect fit, and values of 0.08 or below are considered acceptable. GFI, CFI, TLI, NFI, and RFI take values between 0 and 1; values of 0.95 and above indicate a perfect fit, while values between 0.90 and 0.94 indicate acceptable fit (Hoe, 2008; Kline, 2011; Raykov and Marcoulides, 2006; Şimşek, 2007). The suitability of the model formed in this study was evaluated within the framework of the fit indices mentioned above. The validity and reliability study of the measurement instrument was tested using SPSS 22 and AMOS 22 software at a significance level of .05. Findings  
The validity and reliability study of the measurement instrument consists of two stages. After obtaining the necessary permissions from the author, the measurement instrument was translated into Turkish. Subsequently, the factor structure of the instrument was examined using exploratory factor analysis (EFA) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA). When the CFA results for the Child and Youth Psychological Resilience Scale (CYPRS) are examined, it is found that the t-values and χ2 value are significant at the .01 level. When the χ2 and degrees of freedom values for the fit indices are compared, it is seen that the χ2/df (105.498/52) ratio is 2.03. Examination of the RMSEA value reveals that it has a fit index of .060 (90%, .045-.080). Looking at the other fit indices, GFI is .94, NFI is .94, CFI is .97, and IFI is .97. Regarding the standardized RMR value, the fit index is .039. As a result, the confirmatory factor analysis indicates that the 12-item model demonstrates an adequate level of fit. The standardized parameter values for the Child and Youth Psychological Resilience Scale (CYPRS) obtained as a result of the CFA are presented in Figure 1. Finally, the criterion validity of the measurement instrument was examined in relation to positive and negative affect and self-efficacy. Significant correlations were found: .57 with positive affect, -.39 with negative affect, and .45 with self-efficacy for the CYPRS. In light of these results, it can be said that the scale demonstrates criterion validity. Findings Regarding Reliability  
Within the scope of the reliability study, the Cronbach’s alpha reliability coefficient was calculated for the entire scale. The internal consistency coefficient for the first sample was found to be .91. These values can be considered quite good for a measurement instrument consisting of twelve items. Additionally, as shown in Table 1, the item-total correlation values of the scale range between .45 and .79. The obtained values indicate that this scale is a reliable measurement tool for assessing psychological resilience in children and adolescents. Conclusion, Discussion, and Recommendations  
In this study, the Turkish adaptation of the Child and Youth Psychological Resilience Scale, whose validity and reliability study was conducted by Liebenberg, Ungar, and LeBlanc (2013), was carried out. As part of the validity study, the factor structure was examined. The analysis results showed that the 12 items of the scale were gathered under a single factor. Criterion validity was established through correlations with positive and negative affect and self-efficacy. In the reliability study, the internal consistency level was examined. The findings obtained in this study indicate that the scale can be used as a reliable and valid measurement instrument for children and adolescents in our country as well. The findings related to the exploratory factor analysis revealed that the scale has a structure explaining 51.28% of the total variance, with item factor loadings ranging from .54 to .81. In the original form of the scale, it was found that the factor load values of the items ranged between .39 and .88 (Liebenberg, Ungar, and LeBlanc, 2013). In unidimensional measurement instruments, a variance of 30% or above is considered acceptable. Additionally, factor loadings of .45 or higher are regarded as good (Büyüköztürk, 2010). The findings obtained in this study indicated that the scale has items with high factor loadings, demonstrating strong representation of the construct. For criterion validity, positive and negative affect, as well as self-efficacy, were used. Significant correlations were found: .57 with positive affect, -.39 with negative affect, and .45 with self-efficacy on the Child and Youth Psychological Resilience Scale (CYPRS). Studies have reported that individuals with high self-efficacy tend to have higher levels of psychological resilience (Terzi, 2006; Keye and Pidgeon, 2013), and that resilient individuals possess more positive emotions (Ong, Zautra, and Reid, 2010; Tugade and Fredrickson, 2004). In this context, these findings can be said to support the criterion validity of the scale. The findings related to the reliability study of the scale showed that the internal consistency coefficients calculated for the subscales and for the overall scale were at an adequate level. In the first study, the internal consistency coefficient was calculated as .91. In the study by Liebenberg, Ungar, and LeBlanc (2013), the internal consistency coefficient of the scale was reported as .84. The internal consistency coefficients obtained in the two studies conducted within the scope of the present research are consistent with the results of the original study. In conclusion, the results obtained indicate that the measurement instrument can be used to determine psychological resilience in children and adolescents in our country. The small number of items in the instrument can be considered an advantage for both researchers and participants in practical applications of future studies. Additionally, it is thought that the instrument will make a significant contribution to school psychological counselors in preventive and intervention studies to be developed for students experiencing adverse events during the educational process. Finally, the validity and reliability study of the scale was conducted on a normal population. This situation can be considered a limitation. Therefore, it is believed that conducting studies with risk groups would also be beneficial. The aim of this study is to examine the psychometric properties of the Child and Youth Psychological Resilience Scale. A total of 256 students studying in middle and high schools in the city center of Isparta participated in the study. The ages of the participants ranged from 11 to 16 years. The mean age was 13.05 (SD = .97). Of the participants, 44% were female and 56% were male students. The results of the exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses showed that the scale consists of a single factor that accounts for 51.28% of the total variance. As part of the reliability study, the internal consistency coefficient of the scale was calculated. The Cronbach’s alpha coefficient was found to be .91. These findings indicate that the Child and Youth Psychological Resilience Scale can be used to assess psychological resilience in children and adolescents in our country.

Giriş
Ergenlik dönemin genellikle alan yazında çocukluktan yetişkinliğe geçiş dönemi olarak ele
alınmaktadır (Steinberg, 2007). Bu dönemde bireyde meydana gelen değişimler birey için
birtakım uyum sorunlarını beraberinde getirirken aynı zamanda yeni yaşantılar için fırsatlar
sunar. Bu süreçte birey, gelişim sürecini ve iyi oluşunu olumsuz etkileyebilecek istismar ve
ihmal, boşanma, gibi bir takım yaşantılar ile karşı karşıya kalabilmektedir (Santrock, 2012). Kişinin karşılaşmış olduğu bu zorluklar rağmen sağlıklı şekilde gelişim göstermesi alan
yazında psikolojik sağlamlık kavramı ile karşılık bulmaktadır (Sameroff, 2005).

Introduction  
The period of adolescence is generally addressed in the literature as a transitional phase from childhood to adulthood (Steinberg, 2007). The changes experienced by individuals during this period bring about certain adaptation problems, while also providing opportunities for new experiences. In this process, individuals may be faced with various experiences such as abuse, neglect, or divorce, which can negatively affect their developmental processes and well-being (Santrock, 2012). The healthy development of an individual despite these difficulties is referred to as psychological resilience in the literature (Sameroff, 2005).

discourses.source_txt:
Bireyin olumlu yaşantıları, duyguları, kişilik özellikleri ve deneyimleri ile güçlü
yönleri üzerine odaklanan pozitif psikolojinin ilgilendiği önemli kavramlarından biri olan
psikolojik sağlamlık kavramı, yapılan çalışmalarda gerek kavramsal gerekse metodolojik
açıdan oldukça hetrojen bir yapı göstermektedir (Nasvytienė, La zdauskas ve Leonavičienė,
2012). Zorluklar karşısında gösterilen olumlu uyumu kapsayan ve dinamik bir süreç olarak
tanımlanan psikolojik sağlamlıkta iki önemli durum söz konusudur. Bunlardan birincisi
önemli bir tehdide veya ciddi bir sıkıntıya maruz kalma ve diğeri de gelişimsel sürece yönelik
önemli saldırıları ve travmaları içermesine karşın olumlu uyum sağlamayı başarmadır (Luthar,
2005; Luthar, Cicchetti ve Becker, 2000; Masten, 2001; Masten ve Coatsworth, 1998). Burada
bireyin gelişimine veya uyumuna yönelik tehditlere ya da risklere rağmen olumlu sonuçların
ortaya çıkması söz konusudur (Masten, 2001). Ortak bir tanımdan bahsetmek güç olsa da,
yapılan tanımlardan hareketle psikolojik sağlamlığın olumsuz yaşantılar karşısında bireyin
uyum sağlayabilme ve gelişim sürecini sürdürebilme kapasitesi olduğu söylenilebilir.
discourses.translated_txt: Psychological resilience, one of the key concepts of positive psychology— which focuses on individuals’ positive experiences, emotions, personality traits, and strengths—has been shown in the literature to exhibit considerable heterogeneity both conceptually and methodologically (Nasvytienė, La zdauskas, and Leonavičienė, 2012). Psychological resilience, defined as a dynamic process that encompasses positive adaptation in the face of adversity, involves two important conditions. The first is exposure to a significant threat or serious distress, and the second is the ability to achieve positive adaptation despite facing major developmental threats and traumas (Luthar, 2005; Luthar, Cicchetti, and Becker, 2000; Masten, 2001; Masten and Coatsworth, 1998). Here, positive outcomes emerge despite threats or risks to the individual’s development or adaptation (Masten, 2001). Although it is difficult to speak of a single definition, based on the definitions provided, psychological resilience can be said to refer to an individual’s capacity to adapt and continue their developmental process in the face of adverse experiences.

discourses.translated_txt: The multidimensional and complex structure of the concept of psychological resilience presents significant challenges in evaluating the construct and in developing measurement tools for its assessment (Liebenberg, Ungar, and LeBlanc, 2013). It can be said that this situation necessitates the use of different measurement tools to identify the individual, familial, social, and cultural qualities of resilient individuals. In addition, examining the characteristics of resilient individuals holds a crucial place in terms of preventive and intervention studies. Therefore, it appears that there is a need for new measurement tools to assess psychological resilience in children and adolescents, as indicated in the literature. Furthermore, when the literature is reviewed, it is evident that there are only a limited number of measurement tools available in our country for assessing psychological resilience in children and adolescents. For example, the Psychological Resilience and Adolescent Development Scale, adapted by Gizir and Aydın (2006), was developed to identify protective factors related to psychological resilience. This scale, which consists of internal and external protective factors, includes 56 items.

discourses.translated_txt: Child and Youth Psychological Resilience Scale: The original form of the scale, developed based on data collected from eleven different countries, consists of 28 items, three subscales, and eight subdimensions. The measurement tool was developed using both quantitative and qualitative methods from a socio-ecological perspective (Liebenberg, Ungar, and Van de Vijver, 2012). The short form study of the scale was conducted by Liebenberg, Ungar, and LeBlanc (2013), and as a result of two different studies, a structure consisting of 12 items was obtained. The factor loadings of the scale range between .39 and .88, and its internal consistency coefficient was found to be .84. The measurement tool uses a five-point Likert structure, ranging from “Describes me completely (5)” to “Does not describe me at all (1).” Higher scores indicate a higher level of resilience.

Ölçme aracına ilişkin dil geçerliliği kapsamında 12 maddeden oluşan ölçeğin orijinal İngilizce
formu, ölçeği geliştiren araştırmacıdan izin alınarak, önce araştırmacılar tarafından Türkçe’ye,
daha sonra eğitim bilimleri alanından iki öğretim üyesi tarafından Türkçe’den İngilizce ’ye
çevrilmiş, her iki dili etkili bir şekilde kullanabilen alandan üçüncü bir öğretim üyesi
tarafından çeviriler karşılaştırılarak ölçeğe son şekli verilmiştir. Ölçme araçları 2014-2015
eğitim öğretim dönemi başında farklı ortaokul ve lisede okuyan öğrencilerden gönüllü
olanlara verilerek uygulanmıştır. İlk olarak ili milli eğitim müdürlüğünden araştırmanın
yapılabilmesi için gerekli izinler alınmıştır. Daha sonra rastgele belirlenen okullarda
uygulama sürecine geçilmiştir. Uygulama öncesi katılımcılara araştırmanın amacı ve ölçme
araçları hakkında kısaca bilgi verilmiştir. Verilerin toplanması yaklaşık bir hafta ve uygulama
30 dakika sürmüştür. Elde edilen veriler bilgisayar ortamına aktarıldıktan sonra, yapılacak analizler için
gerekli varsayımlara bakılmıştır. Öncelikle hatalı ve kayıp veriler, frekans dağılımları yardımı
ile incelenmiş, hatalı verilere ilişkin gerekli düzeltmeler yapılmıştır.
discourses.translated_txt:
Data Analysis Process
Within the scope of language validity for the measurement instrument, the original English form of the 12-item scale, with permission from the researcher who developed the scale, was first translated into Turkish by the researchers, and then back into English by two faculty members from the field of educational sciences. A third faculty member from the field, proficient in both languages, compared the translations and finalized the scale. The measurement instruments were administered at the beginning of the 2014–2015 academic year to volunteers among students from various middle and high schools. Initially, the necessary permissions to conduct the research were obtained from the provincial directorate of national education. Subsequently, the implementation process began in randomly selected schools. Prior to administration, participants were briefly informed about the purpose of the research and the measurement instruments. Data collection took approximately one week and the administration lasted 30 minutes. After transferring the collected data to the computer environment, the necessary assumptions for the analyses were examined. First, incorrect and missing data were reviewed with the help of frequency distributions, and the necessary corrections were made for the erroneous data.

discourses.translated_txt: Missing values can be tolerated if they are below 5% and randomly distributed (Acuna and Rodriguez, 2004). Missing values were examined, and 68 datasets with more than 5% missing data were excluded. For missing values below 5%, values were imputed using the arithmetic mean (series mean) to avoid conditions that might affect the normal distribution status of the dataset or the analysis results (Seçer, 2013). In the next step, outliers and the assumption of multivariate normality in the dataset were examined using Mahalanobis distance values, and 12 datasets were removed due to being extreme outliers. Additionally, skewness and kurtosis coefficients were checked for the assumption of univariate normality. It was found that the skewness and kurtosis values met the normality assumption within the range of +1 and -1 (Can, 2013; Morgan, Leech, Gloeckner, and Barrett, 2004). The results of confirmatory factor analysis for the measurement instrument were evaluated within the framework of fit indices, including chi-square (χ2), χ2/df ratio, goodness of fit index (GFI), normed fit index (NFI), comparative fit index (CFI), standardized root mean square residuals (SRMR), incremental fit index (IFI), and root mean square error of approximation (RMSEA). A χ2/df ratio below 3 indicates an acceptable fit, while RMSEA and SRMR values equal to or less than 0.05 indicate a perfect fit, and values of 0.08 or below are considered acceptable. GFI, CFI, TLI, NFI, and RFI take values between 0 and 1; values of 0.95 and above indicate a perfect fit, while values between 0.90 and 0.94 indicate acceptable fit (Hoe, 2008; Kline, 2011; Raykov and Marcoulides, 2006; Şimşek, 2007). The suitability of the model formed in this study was evaluated within the framework of the fit indices mentioned above. The validity and reliability study of the measurement instrument was tested using SPSS 22 and AMOS 22 software at a significance level of .05.

discourses.translated_txt:
Ege Education Journal 2015 (16) 1: 1-12 Psychometric Properties of the Child and Youth Psychological Resilience Scale (ÇGPSÖ-12): Validity and Reliability Study 7 Findings Regarding Validity
Before conducting factor analysis, partial correlations between items and the suitability of the correlation matrix for factor analysis were examined using the Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin (KMO) coefficient and the Bartlett test. The results indicated that the Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin value was .92, and the result of the Bartlett test (χ2 = 1533.522, df = 66, p < .000) was found to be significant. Accordingly, it was accepted that the data were derived from a multivariate normal distribution and that the partial correlations between items and the correlation matrix were suitable for factor analysis. To examine the construct validity and factor structure of the scale, exploratory factor analysis was conducted, and principal components analysis was used as the factoring technique. In determining the construct validity of the scale, factors with eigenvalues above 1.00 according to Kaiser normalization were considered as criteria.

Standardized parameter values for the Child and Youth Psychological Resilience Scale

When the CFA results for the Child and Youth Psychological Resilience Scale (CYPRS) are examined, it is found that the t-values and χ2 value are significant at the .01 level. Findings Regarding Reliability  
Within the scope of the reliability study, the Cronbach’s alpha reliability coefficient was calculated for the entire scale. The internal consistency coefficient for the first sample was found to be .91. These values can be considered quite good for a measurement instrument consisting of twelve items. Additionally, as shown in Table 1, the item-total correlation values of the scale range between .45 and .79. The obtained values indicate that this scale is a reliable measurement tool for assessing psychological resilience in children and adolescents.

Conclusion, Discussion, and Recommendations  
In this study, the Turkish adaptation of the Child and Youth Psychological Resilience Scale, whose validity and reliability study was conducted by Liebenberg, Ungar, and LeBlanc (2013), was carried out. As part of the validity study, the factor structure was examined. The analysis results showed that the 12 items of the scale were gathered under a single factor. Criterion validity was established through correlations with positive and negative affect and self-efficacy. In the reliability study, the internal consistency level was examined. The findings obtained in this study indicate that the scale can be used as a reliable and valid measurement instrument for children and adolescents in our country as well. The findings related to the exploratory factor analysis revealed that the scale has a structure explaining 51.28% of the total variance, with item factor loadings ranging from .54 to .81. In the original form of the scale, it was found that the factor load values of the items ranged between .39 and .88 (Liebenberg, Ungar, and LeBlanc, 2013).

Additionally, factor loadings of .45 or higher are regarded as good (Büyüköztürk, 2010). The findings obtained in this study indicated that the scale has items with high factor loadings, demonstrating strong representation of the construct. For criterion validity, positive and negative affect, as well as self-efficacy, were used. Significant correlations were found: .57 with positive affect, -.39 with negative affect, and .45 with self-efficacy on the Child and Youth Psychological Resilience Scale (CYPRS).

Yapılan çalışmalarda öz yeterliliği yüksek olan
bireylerin psikolojik sağlamlık düzeylerinin daha yükse olduğu (Terzi, 2006; Keye ve
Pidgeon, 2013), sağlam bireylerin daha olumlu duygulara sahip olduklarına ilişkin sonuçlar
rapor edilmiştir (Ong, Zautra ve Reid, 2010; Tugade ve Fredrickson, 2004). Bu bağlamda elde
edilen bu sonuçların ölçeğin ölçüt geçerliliğini desteklediği söylenebilir. Ölçeğin güvenirlik çalışması ile ilgili bulgular, alt ölçekler ve tüm ölçek için
hesaplanan iç tutarlık katsayılarının yeterli düzeyde olduğunu göstermiştir. Birinci çalışmada
elde edilen iç tutarlılık kat sayısı .91 olarak hesaplanmıştır. Liebenberg, Ungar ve LeBlanc
(2013) yaptıkları çalışmada ölçeğin iç tutarlılık katsayısını .84 olarak hesaplamışlardır. Bu
çalışma kapsamında yapılan iki çalışmadan elde edilen iç tutarlılık katsayısı, orijinal
çalışmada elde edilen sonuç ile paralellik göstermiştir.
discourses.translated_txt: Studies have reported that individuals with high self-efficacy tend to have higher levels of psychological resilience (Terzi, 2006; Keye and Pidgeon, 2013), and that resilient individuals possess more positive emotions (Ong, Zautra, and Reid, 2010; Tugade and Fredrickson, 2004). In this context, these findings can be said to support the criterion validity of the scale. The findings related to the reliability study of the scale showed that the internal consistency coefficients calculated for the subscales and for the overall scale were at an adequate level. In the first study, the internal consistency coefficient was calculated as .91. In the study by Liebenberg, Ungar, and LeBlanc (2013), the internal consistency coefficient of the scale was reported as .84. The internal consistency coefficients obtained in the two studies conducted within the scope of the present research are consistent with the results of the original study.

Sonuç olarak elde edilen sonuçlar ülkemizde çocuk ve ergenlerde psikolojik
sağlamlığı belirlemede ölçme aracının kullanılabileceğini göstermektedir. Ölçme aracındaki
madde sayısının az olması, yapılacak araştırmalara ilişkin uygulamalarda araştırmacı ve
katılımcılar açısından avantaj sağladığı söylenebilir. Ayrıca ölçme aracının eğitim-öğretim
süreci içerisinde olumsuz yaşantılar sonrasında öğrencilere yönelik geliştirilecek önleyici ve
müdahale edici çalışmalarda, ölçme aracının okul psikolojik danışmanlarına büyük katkı
sağlayacağı düşünülmektedir. Son olarak ölçeğin geçerlilik ve güvenirlik çalışması normal
popülasyon üzerinde yapılmıştır.
discourses.translated_txt: In conclusion, the results obtained indicate that the measurement instrument can be used to determine psychological resilience in children and adolescents in our country. The small number of items in the instrument can be considered an advantage for both researchers and participants in practical applications of future studies. Additionally, it is thought that the instrument will make a significant contribution to school psychological counselors in preventive and intervention studies to be developed for students experiencing adverse events during the educational process. Finally, the validity and reliability study of the scale was conducted on a normal population.
